Using a Monte Carlo approach, we evaluated the potential of early massive black holes ($M_1=M_2=10^5 M_{\sun}$) formed by Population III stars to coalesce within first-generation stellar clusters at various redshift levels ($0 \le z \le 2$). By generating $10^7$ random orbital configurations characterized by initial separations drawn from a uniform distribution up to 2 AU and eccentricities set to 1, we identified black hole mergers resulting from both direct gravitational wave emission and those caused by loss-cone refills due to stellar dynamical interactions. Our findings indicate that over 90% of Population III binary remnants merge within a $z>0$ timeframe via direct emission. Conversely, roughly 30% merge at redshiftes $z>0$ specifically because of dynamical interactions with stars. By integrating these fractions based on predicted Population III binary merger rates across cosmic history, we determine that the Milky Way's central Nuclear Star Cluster should host at least one merger occurring between $z=2$ and $z=0$. Furthermore, a significant majority of these events are expected to take place before the Milky Way reaches $z=1$, implying that subsequent dynamical encounters within $z<1$ will yield multiple coalescences capable of producing black hole signals through interferometric detectors.

In grid systems featuring Energy Storage Systems (ESS) coupled with sophisticated control mechanisms, conventional monitoring methods struggle to identify malfunctions like device failures. To address this, our research proposes a novel, data-centric framework for pinpointing operational anomalies within islanded microgrids containing ESS. This methodology entails training a supervised classification algorithm on historical data to pinpoint deviations, all while mitigating privacy risks through the application of differential privacy. Distinguished from existing approaches, this scheme eliminates the need for granular load forecasting. Instead, it capitalizes on the inherent fluctuations in load profiles and the dual dimensions of charging and discharging states to furnish sufficient information for robust anomaly detection.

We present an approach for learning single-view 3D object pose estimation by leveraging a new dataset composed of in-the-wild video clips sourced directly from online video platforms. Established object instances were identified within these clips by harnessing existing visual recognition and tracking technologies. We argue that using in-the-wild video offers a dual advantage: it allows for the creation of highly diverse training sets with simple access to such footage, and these natural scenes provide a robust test benchmark for evaluating real-world generalization. To address the technical challenge of synthesizing accurate pose annotations from this source material, we employed state-of-the-art detectors and trackers to extract labeled data exclusively. This method yielded over 1.1 million single-view object instances featuring more than one million unique objects. We evaluated our method against a synthesized test set constructed from identical training material to verify that our single-approach successfully adapts to unseen environments. Results demonstrate a substantial improvement in object pose estimation, particularly when using tests derived from natural video rather than synthetic ones; specifically, our approach achieves over 80% NMS-IOU in the generalization test. For comparison, we achieved 58.9% NMS-IOU on the standard Nike driving dataset test, indicating a strong result on that more challenging benchmark.

Despite significant vaccine efficacy, widespread adoption of COVID-19 shots has been hindered by misinformation. While previous research has addressed such misinformation largely through the lens of health literacy, this study posits that alongside individual cognitive traits, social influences also play a critical role in both believing and dispelling false narratives. To evaluate how susceptibility to and willingness to correct misinformation are influenced by both factors, we administered an online survey featuring twenty misinformation statements alongside corresponding fact-checks. By analyzing responses via an unsupervised machine learning model—without utilizing respondents' initial reaction data for training—we developed an original susceptibility and correction score for each item. Ultimately, we applied a logistic regression framework that confirmed belief in misinformation as driven by health analytics personality dimensions alongside social forces; we further introduced a novel framework detailing the specific belief and correction mechanisms unique to misinformation concerning vaccines.

Attosecond physics holds the potential to capture the most fundamental electronic movements within matter, yet advancements in attosecond techniques are hindered by limitations regarding the spectral range (from infrared to visible light) and the accessibility of the two-dimensional attoclock technique. This study demonstrates the recovery of the attoclock functionality using a combined approach of mid-infrared counter-rotating linearly polarized lasers within a single atomic vapor cell. This methodology achieves two critical objectives: it introduces mid-infrared attoclocks as a previously unexplored technology for measurement, and it enables the broadening of accessible harmonic frequencies to higher energies by employing counter-rotating lasers.

Ephemerides for eclipsing binaries are established via the periodic analysis of observed eclipse events; however, if a system exhibits a significant deviation from strict periodicity, the standard least-squares fitting of a light curve element (like the orbital period) becomes inadequate. For variables with an irregularly drifting period, a general Taylor expansion of the eclipse timing (ET) must be employed instead. We propose a new methodology to determine the elements of this expansion through the direct least-squares fitting of ET residuals, supplemented by numerical simulations to assess this approach's performance. When applied to real systems, we find that this technique yields an element set highly compatible with those derived using classical, non-linear least-squares methods on the light curve itself. Furthermore, our method proves robust even in the presence of additional observational data unrelated to eclipses. Beyond its technical application, we illustrate how this framework aids in distinguishing whether a system's period variability stems from intrinsic changes or observational noise, offering critical insights into complexes like the W UMa-type eclipsing binaries group where simulating non-eclipse events remains a challenge.

Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) represent a promising alternative to conventional numerical methods for solving physics-governed partial differential equations (PDEs). Unlike traditional approaches that rely on mesh-based discretization and operate within finite-dimensional approximation spaces, PINNs utilize neural networks—offering high adaptability for high-level PDEs within a meshless framework. This study provides a comprehensive overview of the latest advances in these neural numerical methods. We begin by reviewing foundational schemes and existing variations for domain problems before examining solutions for boundary value problems (BVPEs) and moving boundary value problems (MBVPEs). Finally, we discuss current research limitations and potential strategies to overcome them.

This paper introduces an automated solution for identifying and remediating security vulnerabilities within the Cargo ecosystem. Our advanced dependency analysis detects specific issues such as redundant packages, redundant checks for package substitution, and redundant substitutions to ensure safety compliance. By generating minimal remediation strategies for every dependency, our approach significantly reduces the number of vulnerable items while applying far fewer changes compared to prior methods when securing cargo projects. Extensive testing confirms that our system works on a substantial number of real-world projects with high precision and performance levels.

Within the context of the Dyson model, we demonstrate ergodicity within specific subregions of parameters space, thereby substantiating the unique ergodicity measure found previously in our investigation of ergodic dynamics for these systems.

Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) utilize local spatial invariance to efficiently learn robust global features, yet this strong invariance often blurs the precise locations of objects. In contrast, solving the "Spatial Localization Problem"—which involves restoring accurate pixel-level object positions given only DCNN predictions—is critical for many applications in Computer Vision. This paper introduces Orientation Convolutional Networks (OCNs), a generalization of DCNNs that retains local spatial mapping. We demonstrate that both image classification and object detection can successfully leverage this architecture to achieve pixel-level accuracy using the DCNN as a coarse estimator followed by OCNs for refinement. Furthermore, our results show that integrating DCNNs and OCNs significantly boosts both classification and detection performance.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) excel at solving problems embedded within graph structures, prompting extensive research into learning on point clouds by first constructing a useful point graph. However, conventional graph convolutional networks (GCNs) suffer from high computational costs during both message passing and aggregation. This paper introduces the Dual-Graph Learning Network (DGLN) to optimize GCN efficiency. By reformulating graph convolution as a matrix multiplication operation, we achieve significant computational speedup. Furthermore, we define a dual-graph framework where one organizes points via spatial proximity and the other via local geometric tangent spaces. Empirical results demonstrate that DGLN not only reduces inference latency by approximately 50% but also enhances representation learning on both tangent graphs. The methodology yields substantial improvements in graph-level classification accuracy and is particularly effective at reconstructing point clouds from partial observations, all while requiring no additional model parameters. Source code is available at: https://github.com/zhengyongjie/DGLN.

A primary objective in exoplanet research is determining the internal composition of terrestrial worlds to reveal insights about their origins and evolutionary histories. A critical component of this internal composition analysis is devolatilisation—specifically, separating volatile elements from refractory components, which are often partitioned by their condensation temperatures. By applying elemental partition coefficients to mass data from exoplanets formed from volatile-poor stellar material, scientists can infer new information about these stars. Conversely, assuming an exoplanet formed from volatile-rich stellar material presents a significant challenge. To isolate the true refractory and volatile-poor core mass under these conditions, a comprehensive mass balance encompassing the entire planet is required. Our findings indicate that devolatilisation during the formation of rocky terrestrial planets in our own Solar System could have resulted in approximately a 10% reduction in the primordial mass of the Sun. Therefore, failing to account for this loss could lead to erroneous conclusions when interpreting the volatile contents of exoplanetary host stars.

Deep neural networks (DNNs), typically leveraging Channel State Information (CSI), have emerged as a leading method for wireless localization. While manually engineered features can introduce errors through the subjectivity of their creation, this study introduces an alternative: automatically extracting channel fingerprints through the layers of a CSI-structured DNN. This approach lays foundation for creating CSI-based localization systems that are more accurate and maintain higher robustness against scattering anomalies and hardware defects.

This study investigates jet fragmentation functions within pp and PbPb contexts at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 2.76$ TeV using the ALICE detector. In pp collisions, the measured jet fragmentation functions demonstrate good alignment with both DigeoJet and PYTHIA 8 simulations. For central PbPb collisions, jet yields show a mild suppression relative to pp collisions, while fragmentation functions exhibit significant modifications with pronounced suppression at high $z$ values. These findings in heavy-ion collisions are consistent with parton energy loss models, such as DigeoJet. Additionally, jet-substructure analyses of PbPb collisions using observables like $\tau_1$, $\sigma_g$, and $N_{ch}$ confirm that these features effectively trace the effects of parton-medium interactions.

The M88 cluster, historically regarded as one of the Hubble's deepest observations, has recently been identified as a potential site of active star formation. This paper investigates two transitless systems within M88 using the Spitzer Space Telescope's IRAC data, which consists of four photometric bands. While one candidate is a free-floating ultra-cool brown dwarf, the other is uniquely a M6Y dwarf, representing only the third known Y dwarf in the Northern Hemisphere. This distant Y dwarf (at approximately 1.8 degrees from the cluster center) was identified through its distinctive Spitzer color indices; notably, its J - H index is atypical for an object with its gravity and temperature classification. Furthermore, the study includes a comprehensive analysis of M88's background stellar population, which was found to be approximately 1.5 times more extensive than previously documented. Due to data limitations, no definitive conclusions were reached regarding the cluster's age, but there is a strong possibility that both detected objects are pre-main-sequence young brown dwarfs.

Our study also reveals that the development of particle-type dependent elliptic flow requires an accompanying increase in radial flow as part of the high-energy heavy-ion collision process.

This study introduces a resolution to classify and segment handwritten single-line math terms using a binary classifier paired with two pre-trained character models. The proposed framework demonstrates superior performance compared to existing state-of_the_art methods in the recognized CROHME-IEEE/PIMS handwriting competition. Math terms within this context encompass subscripts, superscripts, fractions, radicals, exponents, and complex multi-level structures. Despite the novelty of these features in 2012, generic two-pass systems failed to address them effectively, prompting this tailored binary classification approach. Math terms are categorized into four distinct categories based on their structural complexity: (1) normal, (2) with subscripts, (3) with superscripts, & (4) with multi-level expressions. For initial classification, four separate Convolutional Neural Networks were trained on image datasets to determine the term type. Following this classification step, two existing character classifiers—one optimized for baseline writing and the elevated writing style—are deployed to fully segment and recognize the characters within each category. Our generated outcomes surpassed previous submissions to the benchmark dataset by significantly improving accuracy rates (60% improvement over the baseline). The methodology offers significant advancements over prior state-of-the-art methods in recognizing handwritten mathematical symbols.

This paper investigates robust methods for duration modeling in neural speech synthesis. Although standard TTS pipelines utilize a Gaussian likelihood on a duration predictor's mean output, this study explores alternatives based on Bernoulli and Student's t-distributions. We find that using the median (via these distributions) rather than the mean yields greater robustness against outliers without requiring method changes. Specifically, a duration predictor using median estimation proved 3.5 dB less sensitive to added noise than one using mean estimation, achieving comparable word error rates. Although slightly longer synthesized silences occurred with a median-focused model, it significantly improved naturalness when paired with a mean-based model. These results highlight the value of statistical robustness in duration estimation, ultimately suggesting a hybrid strategy that combines a duration predictor targeting the median with a predictor targeting the mean.

Occupancy modeling is a widely employed framework for investigating how environmental variables influence a species' presence or absence; however, inaccuracies in field surveys can result in substantial bias during parameter estimation. Recent efforts have sought to enhance the accuracy of these estimates by incorporating hierarchical information regarding survey effort and environmental gradients, yet such strategies often rely on ecological theories that may not hold universally. This study examines whether improving the accuracy of occupancy models is more effectively achieved by hierarchical efforts to adjust for environmental variables or by simply increasing the total number of surveys per site. Based on theoretical analysis and simulations, we find that reducing bias in occupancy parameters is most successful through increased survey effort, provided efforts are scaled according to effort-dependent functions for both surveying and sampling across all sites—supporting current efforts-based sampling methods. Conversely, increasing survey effort is deemed more effective than adapting survey efforts hierarchically when environmental effort-dependent functions vary spatially. Moreover, we demonstrate through both theory and simulation that final estimates of occupancy and detection are highly resilient whether the total survey effort remains constant or varies depending on site-specific environmental conditions from the hierarchical process.

The critical need for precise diagnosis, effective treatment, and proactive prevention has driven the application of deep neural networks (DNLs) across numerous medical domains, including dermatology. While these networks have demonstrated success in automated classification of skin lesions via extensive datasets and iterative retraining, their interaction with clinical practitioners remains limited. We introduce FLAVER, an interactive deep learning framework designed for assessing melanoma. By combining an attention-guided explanation mechanism with interactive label correction, the system not only visualizes prediction confidence but also facilitates tailored diagnostic adjustments based on specific clinical inputs. FLAVER was validated using a cohort of 535 patients from the MEDISIM trial; unlike static DNLs which achieved only 75.6% accuracy on this previously unseen test set, FLER raised performance to 82.7%. These results underscore that the proposed interactive paradigm is capable of delivering robust diagnostic assistance in real-world clinical settings.

We introduce a probabilistic autoencoder (PAE) based on a two-layer architecture designed specifically for physically parameterizing Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia). This generalization incorporates a non-deterministic model of extinction, informed by the probabilistic nature of the Bernoulli likelihood combined with complex entropy. By applying this framework to synthetic spectral time series data, the model successfully recovers the intrinsic parameters and extinction characteristics. Additionally, it successfully identifies a previously unknown physical configuration involving mild, complete extinction that remains position-independent within the training data set.

Disease transmission models using contact graphs typically represent interactions as pairwise edges between individuals, often overlooking significant real-world complexities. This study introduces an alternative approach using hypergraphs to capture multi-way contacts that simultaneously affect groups of people. The authors analyze the critical contact number—the threshold for disease outbreak initiation—within a stochastic susceptible-exposed-infectious-removed (SEIR) model based on these contact hypergraphs. They prove that as population size grows toward infinity, the stochastic model's critical contact number converges to a specific finite value predicted by a deterministic mean-field infectious disease model. A distinctive feature of this mean-field model, which involves two types of percolation (standard percolation on a configuration model and 2-type dependent percolation), is that predicting outbreak thresholds requires accounting for infections originating from both single infections introduced by one infectives to a group and multiple infections introduced by several infectives within the same group. Additionally, the authors provide sufficient conditions ensuring a unique solution exists for the stationary distribution when no outbreak occurs. Numerical simulations are then used to illustrate and validate the theoretical findings.

The recent discovery of two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors, exemplified by CrI$_3$, has spurred significant interest due to the opportunities they provide on the frontier where magnetism and quantum phenomena converge in novel states. Central to exploring these advanced phases is understanding magnetic coupling across isolated layers. However, interactions derived from magnetic canting—previously considered negligible because of screening effects in bulk materials—may emerge with substantial impact when a near-vacuum barrier separates the layers. This work introduces a comprehensive framework for analyzing such effects and demonstrates their clear presence within CrI$_3$. Specifically, we find that a canting of order $\sim10^1$ rad enhances the antiferromagnetic interlayer coupling by approximately 50%, a modification driven entirely by spin canting. Given their potential to significantly alter interactions, these effects offer highly adjustable control over emerging phenomena, particularly antiferromagnetic spin electronics and twisted magnetism.

This study utilizes 3D magnetohydrodynamic simulations to investigate differential rotation within various rotating, magnetized stratified spheres. Our model incorporates controllable parameters such as the Coriolis force, centrifugal forces, magnetic Parker spiral geometry, and rotation rate, defined via the Rossby number. Key to generating internally coupled dynamical dynamo systems, these variables influence flow dynamics. A particularly notable discovery is that for low values of $Ro < 0.001$, the differential rotation can deviate from classical solar patterns, exhibiting a shift in polarity in radial meridional planes. Additionally, we examine rotation profiles across several $Ro$ values and identify additional solar-like characteristics within specific ranges, namely $0.001 < Ro < 0.01$. These findings offer critical insights for understanding solar and stellar dynamics more broadly.

Although multimodal input is increasingly common, building multibranch deep architectures introduces significant complexity. To address this, we introduce the $K$-Fan model, featuring a multibranched design capable of handling $\textit{K}$ distinct inputs. Each branch employs $\textit{K}$ + a new normalization layer called LAM (Linear Alignment Module) to align features from other branches, while also supporting efficient inference with a computational cost of $\textit{OF}(K\cdot \textit{G})$. This design has been applied to create LAM-based versions for both ResNet and Cross. Tests show that the model outperforms all baselines across eight tasks, including image classification, object detection, keypoint detection, semantic segmentation, and retrieval. Additionally, ablation studies on input count and feature fusion strategies in CWA-ResNet demonstrate strong performance gains.

Model-based checking serves as an established formal verification technique for programs that unit and functional tests fail to validate when threading is involved. This report presents a proposal for enhancing the feasibility of applying model-based checking to larger-scale programs by employing conformance testing. Specifically, we integrate the generation of effective testing sequences, inherited from conformance testing strategies, into the model-checking framework. By utilizing these carefully constructed sequences to explore a target program's behavior, we can significantly diminish the effective state-space, thereby rendering formal verification more practical to implement.

WhatsApp currently holds the distinction of the world's most popular messaging application, facilitating massive information dissemination through its closed network structure. Unfortunately, this environment supports a rapid propagation of fake news, which can cause significant disruption across various sectors by misleading large numbers of people, all while maintaining an opaque trail due to the message's one-to-one delivery system. While existing falsehood detection systems typically depend on weak features like top-ranked misinformation from fact-checkers or user engagement metrics (such as reactions and shares) that encourage deception, we introduce a novel approach that leverages advanced feature extraction to build comprehensive knowledge graphs for identifying deception. By training on a dataset of over 22,000 messages collected from WhatsApp groups in Spain, we demonstrate that our method achieves an accuracy of 88.88% and a balanced F1-score of 84.84%.

The primary goal of spoofing detection systems is to identify synthetic artifacts embedded in speech resulting from synthesis or conversion processes. This paper introduces the incorporation of attention rectified linear units (AReLU) into end-to-end detection pipelines. By leveraging the attention mechanism within ARe LU to emphasize significant acoustic cues and filter out redundancy, the proposed architecture directs model sensitivity toward synthetic artifacts. Tested on the Logical Access Spoorking in Speech (LASP) corpus, which involves a human classifier creating synthetic signals, the model achieved an equal error rate (EER) of 5.76%. This represents superior performance compared to the baseline multilayer perceptron (MLP), which recorded an EER of 7.30%.

Building inflationary models within supergravity is fraught with challenges due to the framework's high degree of flexibility. This summary reviews recent efforts to address these issues by reformulating supergravity using algebraic methods, a shift that clarifies the structure and exposes potential pitfalls. Following an introduction to standard supergravity and its pitfalls, the presentation reformulates the theory in terms of chiral superfields and globally defined vector multiplets, enabling a straightforward generalization to scenarios with multiple scalar fields—a common requirement for realistic inflation models. Specific sections detail the derivation of a K\"ahler potential and analysis within this new formalism, exploration using a locally symmetric approach to symmetric scalar spaces relevant for inflation, examination of how gauge interactions modify these dynamics, and examination of global transformations that influence low-energy effective theories, particularly regarding symmetry breaking via the K\"ahler potential or right-handed neutrino masses.

Nonreciprocal optical systems are widely used to manipulate the signal transmission of light, but existing nonreversible components lack a demonstrated link to quantum entanglement in energy-time correlations of twin photons. This study reevaluates nonreversible optical setups and constructs a novel nonreversible device specifically for four-wave interaction from typed fibers to investigate entanglement non-time-continuity. Experimental results demonstrate that as the direction of twin-photon entanglement changes, nonreciprocal devices can alter specific entanglement degrees of the system. Furthermore, nonreciprocal optical systems can modify a different type of optimal quantum efficiency by using a small amount of twin-photon entanglement time. These nonreciprocal optical components provide new methods for the study of quantum optics and applications related to quantum information technology.

Superconducting quantum circuits are currently the leading platform for quantum mechanics experiments and the development of quantum information processing devices. As circuit quantum electrodynamics (CQED) systems scale up, material imperfections—specifically those in the dielectric components—act as a significant bottleneck, limiting further growth and optimal device design. Recently, fully two-dimensional planar superconducting quantum circuits have emerged as a promising alternative to more complex three-dimensional variants or hybrid systems. This study utilizes a purely two-dimensional design to demonstrate highly efficient coherent coupling between a transmons qubit and an on-chip microwave resonator through space, overcoming previously unattained levels of coupling strength in terms of coherency. Achieving optimal coherency requires meticulous management of dielectric losses within the fabrication process; our results show that fabricated resonators exhibit quality factors ($Q^*$) exceeding $5 \times 10^6$, which represents a substantial improvement over the best prior coherent rates. This performance indicates that dielectric fabrication approaches are nearing their potential limits, establishing a new record for two-dimensional planar circuits. These demonstration results provide a robust foundation for scaling up quantum information processing capabilities while confirming that deeply entangled, multi-qubit quantum states can be reliably constructed within this architecture.

Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs) are highly profitable investment strategies grounded in technical analysis, yet the specific market forces enabling this success remain elusive. In response to the observation that short-term reversal traders also achieve significant profitability, we investigate the similarities between these groups and the trade executions of CTAs. Analyzing over a decade of high-frequency data from the E-mini S&P 500 Futures to capture the timing and structural nuances of CTA activity, our findings reveal distinct daily patterns in CTA trading that short-term reversal traders fail to mirror. By constructing a simplified execution strategy designed to emulate the most profitable aspects of both the CTA and reversal approaches, we isolate specific execution tactics driving CTA success that go beyond standard short-term reversal effects.

Protocol detection involves the critical network security task of identifying protocols transmitted within encrypted payloads, yet existing approaches struggle due to the limited representativeness of available datasets and the inconspicuous nature of protocol-specific signatures. This paper introduces **DeepProtoNet**, a deep learning framework designed to enhance protocol identification by efficiently handling distinctive features across various layers. Distilled from an initial feature analysis revealing significant differences in how protocols manifest, the authors implemented the **Adaptive Multi-Feature Fusion (AMFF)** mechanism. AMFF dynamically evaluates and integrates layers including packet length, lengthened packets, and TCP headers to optimize detection performance. Additionally, a novel **Feature Normalization Layer (FNL)** was developed within DeepProtoNet to standardize numerical representations, thereby boosting training efficiency and convergent speed. To further fortify the model, **DropLayer** leverages the redundancy of accumulated feature dimensions to introduce random noise, which improves generalization and robustness. Extensive experiments using a new, large-scale dataset comprising over 1.33 million samples demonstrate that this proposed method consistently outperforms current state-of-the-art solutions.

Generating a coherent bunch of single-quantum excitations, or Fock states, is essential for advancing magnons as reliable carriers of information alongside other spin-based systems. Because magnons naturally lack negative decay phases required for self-organization into Fock states without a source of phase randomness, previous efforts have struggled. Previous attempts relied on inhomogeneous ensembles subject to decoherence or required external phase-locking mechanisms that fail to truly demonstrate intrinsic coherence. Addressing this gap, our work presents the direct creation of Fock states in a uniform magnet placed in a static dipolar field using only optical pumping. This approach eliminates the need for complex phase-locking setups and overcomes the limitations associated with disorder in unmagnetized samples, thereby establishing a new pathway for creating high-coherence spin-based states.

This Letter introduces a theoretical framework designed for comprehensive optical analysis of high-dimensional Greenberger-Horne-Zeinberger (GHZ) resources. The study initially validates this methodology through complete measurements of distinct three-photon GHZ states within a tripartite quantum basis. The approach is subsequently generalized, with a full photonic hyper-entanglement and quantum Fourier transform integration. The utility of this proposal extends towards enhanced multi-photon capabilities for both quantum computing and quantum communications in higher-order dimensions of entanglement.

This study investigates uplink channel estimation within intelligent-reflecting-surface (IRS)-assisted multi-user systems operating with generic reflection coefficients. Unlike the standard approach, we do not adopt maximum likelihood estimation, even with its variants, as our primary method because Bayes-mle is computationally demanding. Instead, we propose a novel, low-complexity alternative based on the Expectation-C maximization (em) framework. Specifically, we formulate an m algorithm that effectively updates user channel and IRS phase parameters. To ensure practical implementation, we simplify the general m step by developing a direct closed-form solution for the immediate update rules derived from its expectations. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that this proposed closed-form m scheme achieves near-parity performance against the maximum m method while exhibiting significantly reduced computational complexity.

We conducted a content analysis of 1,000 weeks of local news coverage during the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic to assess how it correlated with national metrics for cases, deaths, and news volume. Our data indicates that local news coverage of COVID-19 lagged by approximately two weeks behind national death rates but moved ahead by one to two weeks relative to national case counts; however, this correlation weakened significantly as the pandemic progressed. Additionally, we observed that local news volume rose more than proportionally in relation to national rates, while the proportion of articles dedicated to coronavirus topics increased less than proportionally as death and case counts rose. Although the intensity of local coverage was generally higher than the national average regarding hits per article, these articles tended to be briefer than the national average. Furthermore, most articles contained very few links to other sources. These patterns suggest that as the crisis deepened, such local reporting became increasingly formulaic and repetitive, offering little incremental or useful information to readers.

Bloom filters are highly efficient data structures that utilize a fixed amount of memory to manage set elements with a constant false positive rate. Despite this limitation, they widely serve as a foundational component in high-throughput systems. Cuckoo filters emerged as a significant alternative a decade ago, enabling the release of constant false positive rates by using slightly more memory. This paper introduces a fully release-based Compresssion Bloom Filter variant, termed the Compresssion Cuckoo Filter, which leverages the Inverse Compresssion Hashing function to further enhance efficiency. The memory usage of this new structure is independent of neither the total query volume nor the volume of inserted items. This study introduces FLVAE (Federated Learning Variational Autoencoder) as a novel framework in federated learning (FL) capable of robustly countering Byzantine attacks while rigorously maintaining user privacy. The approach establishes an implicit data encoding during the encoding of each split-data through the latent representation, eliminating the need for explicit data transmission or storage on the server. Furthermore, it certifies data authenticity by evaluating the reconstruction error between original encoded data and that generated via an autoencoder after horizontal federated learning. The work provides theoretical proofs indicating the consistency of the FLVAE estimator under both i.i.d. and non-i.id distribution assumptions. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed estimator across diverse data configurations and its resilience against various attack vectors.

We propose a robust, end-to-end framework for training autonomous driving systems using graphical models and reinforcement learning. The graphical structure integrates an end-to-end policy that converts sensor data directly into control commands with a logical interpreter to enforce high-level constraints derived from formal rules and local-level policies or global strategies that local enforcement cannot cover. We demonstrate this framework by applying it to the creation of a vehicle that navigates urban scenes on the autonomous driving simulation platform, Drive2. The system enables us to navigate the simulator while adhering to complex traffic rules and safety margins, beyond the capabilities of pure safety filters or raw strategies in isolation. By graph-theoretical approaches from model-based control, we show theoretical evidence that our proposed method enables effective achievement of both objectives. In practical experiments, the synthesized driving strategies significantly surpass human-level performance on Drive2, demonstrating the efficacy of our proposed approach in achieving superior results on Drive2. Recent leaps in deep learning catalysis notable advancements in deepfake creation, generating perceptively authentic forgeries of media including images, sequences, and voices. While such innovations bring significant benefits, they also expose critical security vulnerabilities, ushering in substantial risks including misinformation and fraudulent deception. The identification and subsequent atmospheric characterization of sub-Neptune-sized exoplanets have established them as promising candidates for habitability assessments. Nevertheless, the habitability of these worlds is not guaranteed; it depends on whether their internal structure allows for a surface layer of liquid water and if atmospheric conditions support life. This study presents new 3D models addressing both the internal structure and atmospheric evolution of these planets to establish a framework for habitability analysis under diverse conditions. Leveraging the discovered exoplanetary population enables predictions across the required parameters. Specifically, we explore the relationship between the core mass fraction and initial hydrogen/helium opacity to determine the prevalence of habitable worlds. By evaluating the frequency of planets capable of supporting liquid water, we demonstrate the potential for a large number of habitable sub-Neptunes and propose targeted strategies for verifying their atmospheres using current and upcoming observatories.

We introduce a model of a one-dimensional sequence-learnable spiking neuronal network that relies on local learning rules. In this configuration, connections from one set of neurons to the subsequent position involve stronger weights than the reverse, reflecting directional sequencing. Strictly local Hebbian learning rules govern synaptic plasticity. While these rules, in isolation, fail to produce sequence-specific patterns due to an asymmetry in connections between adjacent spiking neurons that allows forward sequences to play out. However, by incorporating the temporal gap between consecutive activity episodes into the Hebbian update rule, we enable long-term memory formation. This system reliably learns and executes specific movement patterns between two such states over time. Introduction of additional modifications allows for more complex plastic rules to produce more efficient learning by producing shorter times to reach a target state after playing. Specifically, we observe that similar to a anti-Hebbian component within our proposed plastic rules, long-term strengthening can occur through the interaction of current spikes with prior historical data. This historically informed anti-Hebbian term speeds up learning. Despite these differences, both approaches ultimately yield the same result: a sequence of efficient transitions driven by plasticity.

This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the challenges inherent in training state-of-the-art Optical Character Recognition (OCR) models to handle unseen scene text instances. We introduce a new framework, BootOCR, which enables an OCR system trained on limited data to continuously learn character classes and writing systems while exposed to infinite, unseen text scenarios. Central to this work is a unified model capable of transcribing arbitrary unknown characters or foreign text; this capability leverages a transcrption-by-translation mechanism and a unified loss function designed to manage both character-level and translation-based tasks. Additionally, we implemented specific engineering solutions to detect diversity within batch training data so that the model can effectively instance-batch adapt to diverse, unseen scenarios. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that both BootOCR and an advanced baseline model outperform previous state-of-the-art results on benchmarks such as ASIA, ASIA Hard, ASIA Research, COCO-Text, RCTW, and COCO Trans Pro.

Generalized polynomial chaos (gPC) expansion serves as a prevalent technique for enhancing the efficiency of solving differential equations by managing dimensionality. Utilizing arbitrary differential operators, this method transforms differential problems into algebraic equations to achieve an order of dimensionality reduction. Although widely celebrated for its computational efficiency, existing approaches have largely overlooked the issue of numerical stability. This research investigates how stability can be incorporated into gPC via a QR decomposition method. Furthermore, we analyze the stability of this proposed approach by examining its energy norm and apply it to derive solutions for second-order ordinary differential equations featuring non-constant coefficients, while also providing a means of assessing energy conservation. Energy conservation, combined with the energy method, is a necessary condition for ensuring that a differential approach remains stable.

The analysis of monitoring multidimensional data has become a critical area in industrial applications. Next, we develop an innovative data reconstruction approach within a reduced space by utilizing the turn-taking sparsity of the graph. Finally, we apply a reduced-dimensional space to monitor operations effectively. The validity of this proposed method has been confirmed through a case study of guava fruit quality assessment.

Building accurate automatic extraction models for visual-heavy documents, such as invoices, is significantly hampered by the expensive collection of thousands of annotated samples. In this work, we present an end-to-end framework for invoice key value extraction that reduces the need for annotated data by leveraging a pooling strategy to isolate reusable visual patterns. By applying specialized convolutional pooling layers inspired by template matching, we identify consistent structures despite variations in font, layout, or camera angle. This method enables us to construct a highly accurate auto-annotation system for invoice fields, such as dates and totals, which generates reliable pseudo-labels for human verification. Using these generated labels, we train a robust end-per-end framework that we validate using both a new public invoice dataset and performance metrics showing improved accuracy over previous methods on existing benchmarks.

The potential of creating an artificial spintronics heterostructure using an antiferromagnetic epitaxial EuS film deposited on paramagnetic (or magnetically adjusted) InAs is explored. This analysis evaluates stability across four distinct orientations of the EuS crystal relative to the InAs substrate to ensure effective epitaxial growth. Results indicate that while the EuS valence band maximum (VBM) aligns slightly below the InAs VBM in all configurations, the energy offset varies between 0.04 and 0.12 eV depending on the specific orientation. Furthermore, the EuS band gap remains largely invariant, measuring between 16–16.4 eV irrespective of the configuration, whereas the InAs band gap decreases from 0.51 eV to a minimum of 0.42 eV in one configuration. Bader charge calculations demonstrate that the electronic charge distribution on Eu atoms stays nearly constant regardless of orientation, while on InAs it varies between -0.17 e to -0.22 e. These findings suggest that optimized EuS/InAs configurations can facilitate spin-polarized tunneling, a prerequisite for constructing functional spintronics devices.

The detection of gravitational waves by LIGO and Virgo has confirmed the existence of binary mergers within three categories: stellar-mass black holes, stellar-mass neutron binars, and combinations of these black holes. Although current detectors have not yet observed neutron-star or mixed systems, their potential presence necessitates advanced signal-injection tests for multi-component mergers. These tests are vital for validating that our understanding of source populations and our ability to identify them can handle complex configurations. Drawing inspiration from recent work on nested sampling for Bayesian parameter estimation in binary mergers, this study introduces an extension designed to handle neutron-star–black hole mergers. We detail the necessary modifications to this new algorithm and demonstrate its effectiveness through extensive injection tests across binary black hole-neutron star populations, successfully recovering accurate parameters alongside reliable Bayesian inference results.

The discovery of the giant planet metallicity correlation prompted numerous investigations into its underlying physical mechanisms. To help clarify this relationship, we present the first systematic study utilizing a homogeneous dataset of 1,086 giant planets drawn from the Kepler mission. Both binary and single systems were analyzed with particular attention to host star metallicity [Fe/H]. Our findings indicate no correlation between [Fe/H] and either planet mass or radius; we explore the statistical implications of the observed excess host metal richness. By reviewing current theories in conjunction with these results, we propose that while giant planet formation depends on metallicity, the subsequent abundance of heavy elements within the host star is not a determining factor. This suggests that the [Fe/H]-mass trend arises from a selection effect, likely due to observational biases.

Naviging complex, dynamic indoor environments demands a robotic platform that supports continuous work while providing perception systems capable of modulating their operations based on current requirements. Fluctuating real-world conditions—such as dust accumulation or specific lighting scenarios—can degrade sensor performance, rendering standard strategies for navigation task execution ineffective. This paper introduces a modular framework for a navigation task that employs varying sensor modalities according to dynamic environmental assessments. We detail the overall system architecture, including a reactive, state-machine-based control scheme capable of integrating different perception modules, alongside specific components such as the reactive control mechanism, the navigation state machine, and the criteria used to trigger modality switches. Furthermore, we present initial results from simulated environments to validate our approach.

The generalized Polya theorem establishes that the Gaussian measure on the real line corresponds to the property equidistributing any monomial against a linear form of pairwise independent, identically distributed random variables. The provided presentation details the complete characterization of \(\alpha\)-adic solenoids satisfying an analogous version of Polya's result for this measure space. The proof relies fundamentally on the solution of particular functional differential equations, where the solutions are continuous and strictly defined positive definite transformations within the group of characters for each given \(\alpha\)-adic solenoid.

Presence-absence information is prevalent in ecological data, yet the analysis and interpretation challenges it poses have only recently begun to receive systematic attention. This essay introduces a coherence-based framework for modeling and understanding such data coherently. Drawing inspiration from a coherent risk measure defined over vector-valued random variables, we formulate a general Coherence Model. Within this structure, a presence/absence outcome is interpreted as exceeding or remaining beneath a specific threshold relative to a random variable of interest. We demonstrate how classical combinatorial constraints can be derived from fundamental axioms of coherence and show the derivation of common logit and normal models as well-fitting special cases. Subsequently, we expand the framework to accommodate multivariate entities, enabling the exploration of correlations among hidden variables. Finally, utilizing simulation data, we show that our proposed approach effectively captures inherent pattern complexity while providing meaningful interpretations of ecological relationships.

Saliency detection stands as a critical computer vision challenge because it enables the system to identify the most significant objects within an image. While current leading methods are highly effective, a significant limitation remains: the inaccurate, one-to-one mapping of detected salient objects to their real-world meanings. To overcome this, we introduce a novel framework that integrates contextual information directly into the detection process. Specifically, our proposed Network Architecture incorporates an advanced, learned semantic representation of the entire image via a Cross-Attention Context Extraction (CACE) module. This mechanism functions similarly to how human cognition works, effectively guiding the detection process by having the system focus on semantically relevant areas while filtering out irrelevant ones. Furthermore, the model performs cross-domain attention to align image-level semantics strictly with local regions. By harmonizing global semantic knowledge with detailed object-level analysis, our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard SOD benchmarks, delivering superior results unmatched by existing techniques.

A palindromic number N is defined as a positive integer whose binary form remains identical when read forwards or backwards. Through the study of quotients formed by dividing one such number by another, we explore several fundamental questions concerning the arising rational and integer values. Specifically, we provide explicit formulas for the binary digits of these results and derive a formula for their exact number of binary digits. Using this latter result, we demonstrate for all valid N and M that the ratio is palindromic in binary if and only if the floor of the quotient is palindromic in binary.

Computed Tomography (CT) relies on measuring X-ray transmission through objects at various angles to reconstruct cross-sectional images of their internal structure. However, polyenergetic X-ray beams can introduce artifacts due to energy-dependent linear attenuation, preventing accurate image quality. While iterative algorithms have been explored to address these issues, they remain vulnerable to noise and lack true quantitative reliability. This work introduces a novel iterative reconstruction framework based on the Widely Cascaded Markovian Multi-Energy Model (WCMMEM). By employing iterative maximum likelihood estimation, the method retrieves cross-sectional images representing the probability density functions (PDFs) of linear coefficients (PDF-LCs), which depict how much material with a specific density exists at every voxel, rather than the attenuation values used in conventional CT images. Initially, a WCMMEM is developed to establish a precise link between physical material properties and X-ray data acquisition, using finite difference methods to derive exact numerical differentiation formulas. Subsequently, a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)-accelerated, density-based algorithm is developed capable of handling large-scale CT datasets by enforcing strict non-negativity of density values. Furthermore, the inclusion of partial differential equation (PDE) smoothing within this model promotes both continuity in density maps and edge preservation.

This study presents the first successful application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to recognize handwritten historical texts in a low-resource environment. Specifically, we successfully developed a system for recognizing historical handwritten mathematical notation using only 1,250 training samples for each class. To achieve this, we utilized an unsupervised data augmentation strategy and integrated multiple technical components, including an Adaptive Training Batch Strategy, unsupervised pre-training, data re-balancing, the CNN architecture, and a carefully designed loss function.

This research introduces a fully integrated CMOS temperature sensor designed for intensive on-chip thermal monitoring in systems that support dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS). This research investigates the online Euclidean spanner problem specifically on the unit interval. Classifying IoT devices is essential for maintaining IoT network security. In recent times, numerous attempts have been made to develop automated detection systems using machine learning. These systems typically require collecting and sharing data about device features to cloud environments to train models and support real-time classification. Nevertheless, two critical issues arise with this approach: (1) transferring data over the cloud consumes power and degrades performance due to increased power consumption and communication costs, particularly for resource-constrained devices, and (2) cloud-based solutions compromise local data privacy. Consequently, we introduce a novel, privacy-preserving framework designed to minimize power usage during IoT device classification. This system utilizes a decentralized architecture featuring a single, fully trained classifier hosted on the cloud alongside numerous edge classifiers at the device level. Each IoT unit locally extracts features from incoming traffic based on shared model parameters provided by the cloud instance, thereby preventing both data transmission and privacy risks. We evaluated this framework using a deep neural network trained on the widely adopted IoT dataset within a simulated environment. Results demonstrate that our method is feasible and effective, reducing power consumption by approximately 90% compared to traditional schemes that transmit all feature data to the cloud.

G\"odel modal logics extend intuitionistic modal logic by incorporating the G\"odel \(\Pi\)-rule, which deduces \(\phi \to \top\) directly from \(\phi^\tau\). In contrast, this work focuses on defining G\"odel modal logics within the context of prepartial orderings by integrating \(\Pi\)-rules into the standard axioms and rules for positively and negatively defined modal logic. We introduce a systematic method to construct the corresponding characteristic semantics for these logics, extending the familiar Kripke semantics used in classical modal logic. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that the resulting logics, together with their inherent axioms, both encompass all previously known 3-valued intuitionistic prepartial orderings and can be fully specified by their respective signature axioms.

A significant benefit of Multi-Align is its flexibility; because it combines alignment with translation, any statistical or neural approach can be utilized at the translated stage. The authors evaluate the model using standard metrics on the Dev2008 dataset, demonstrating improved performance over existing methods. Furthermore, applying Multi-Align with neural alignment mechanisms yields substantial gains over both neural and baseline statistical approaches.

Comprising a micro-optical array and a total-internal-reflection prism, these devices function by converting incident orthogonal linear illumination beams into concentrated, orthogonal linear spots on any 3D surface. The rheology of complex liquids is highly sensitive to interfacial roughness conditions. By combining computational fluid dynamics with a contact dynamics framework, this study examines how various rough surfaces influence shear flow within narrow gaps. We employ a periodic arrangement of rough asperities on a moving wall contacting a stationary periodic rough surface, analyzing complex flow by using a periodic rough geometry on one wall. We identify three distinct friction regimes in these scenarios: a smooth-like flow with minor shifts and increased drag, a surface-specific response characterized by pronounced velocity shifts and elevated shear forces, and an anti-slip velocity profile marked by systematic vorticity and the dominant shear action. These findings are validated using experimental data from parallel plate rheometers featuring patterned rough surfaces. Furthermore, we investigate how varying roughness correlation lengths and amplitude distribution affect flow responses across the various friction regimes.

We systematically examine the constraints on cosmological inflation's classical oscillations generated by recent $\beta$-function calculations. Utiluing both perturbative QCD and two-loop QED $\beta$-function expressions, we evaluate how classical oscillations in fundamental couplings—specifically the strong ($\alpha_s$) and electromagnetic ($\alpha$) charges—affect various fundamental constants and energy scales. Our perturbative QCD analysis indicates that even with current precision limits on the Strong Force coupling, the Strong-Maxwell (SM) transition scale can only be determined within a $\sim25\%$ uncertainty margin. In contrast, two-loop QED calculations suggest that the electromagnetic coupling, precise to about $127$ parts per million, yields an estimated SM transition scale of roughly $154.62$ GeV, deviating by approximately $8.7\%$ from the Standard Model prediction. We further investigate how these classical variations influence the Jarlskog parameter and associated CP violation interactions. Ultimately, these fluctuations in fundamental parameters impose intricate constraints on inflationary models and the dynamics of the early universe.

We investigate the diffusion of a quantum state through one-dimensional lattice sites within the framework of a three-branch wavepacket spreading quantum walk. The system involves a coin operator defined by parameters, including a phase $\phi$ and a mixing angle $\theta_{\text{c}}$. Numerical simulations reveal two distinct regimes governed by $\theta_{\text{c}}$: when the mixing angle is small, the walk evolves into a localized state where the initial packet spreads over only a few lattice sites; conversely, large values of $\theta_{\text{c}}$ result in a diffusive quantum walk. In numerical experiments with $\theta_{\text{c}}=\pi/2$ (implying $\phi=0$), the evolution mirrors the standard Maxwellian coin case, where the coin operator has a symmetric real-valued structure. Under these standard mixing conditions, we derive an analytical formula for the reduced density matrix of the walk and employ it to compute the entanglement entropy between the coin and the walk's direction. Specifically, we analyze the initial rate of change of this entanglement entropy right after state preparation. Furthermore, by introducing an auxiliary parameter $s$ into a generalized coin operator, we examine the evolution of entanglement entropy and its sensitivity to $s$.

Recent advancements in text-conditioned generative diffusion models have made creating high-quality, varied images from text prompts accessible. Despite this, directly optimizing or editing existing images within this framework remains difficult because modifying an existing image while preserving its structure requires distinct characteristics compared to generating one from scratch. To address this, we introduce **SEGA** (Semantic Guidance for Generation and Editing), a unified approach that simplifies both tasks by aligning them through a common intermediate representation. SEGA works by mapping input images into a latent "shape space" while simultaneously learning a corresponding functional "prompt space," thereby decoupling what an image looks like from how it is described. During generation, SEGA uses the synthesized shape image as a reference to guide content creation; during editing, it serves as a structural prior to direct the generation of new content while maintaining the original image's composition. Experiments demonstrate that SEGA is versatile and robust, particularly for difficult domains. Code will be released at: https://github.com/kyus1992/SEGA.

This field has quickly become a prominent focus within computer vision, aiming to enhance prediction accuracy by processing future frames using recent historical data—a concept analogous to Transformer-based Vision Swin. This study integrates the Video Swin-Transformer architecture into a comprehensive framework for creating a non-hierarchical, hierarchical model capable of weather prediction through the integration of multi-scale data. The resulting architecture, named HTransformer, employs a Transformer-based Vision Swin design to forecast the evolution of weather systems by analyzing high-resolution, multi-temporal, and multi-scale satellite imagery. HTransformer demonstrates robust generalization across diverse datasets, including the EarthObservation Dataset, the EarthObservation2 Dataset, and the EarthObservation3 Dataset. By analyzing its performance on these varied data sources, the study provides insights into the transformer's adaptability. Ultimately, these insights confirm that HTransformer achieves outstanding results in the task of predicting future weather states.

Intracellular transport mechanisms are essential for delivering vital molecules throughout neurons. As the most extensive cells in the body, they rely on precise spatio-temporal regulation of cargo delivery to ensure survival and functional integrity. Our study introduces a new approach by applying Wavenet, an advanced deep learning model designed for time series forecasting, to predict the fate of individual endosomes within established neuronal endomembrane networks. Using experimental endomembrane tracking data from a well-characterized network to train and validate the model, our results demonstrate superior performance over existing forecasters in both one-step (immediate next state) and multi-step (subsequent trajectories up to 12 steps) predictions. Notably, the multi-step forecasts successfully reproduce biologically plausible features, including localized endosome accumulation and propagation over long distances. This capability suggests that endomembrane networks function as evidence-guided guided particles. Furthermore, the capacity of Wavenet to infer outcomes based on current states alone highlights its potential utility in networks constrained by missing experimental data points, offering a powerful tool for advancing our understanding of complex endomembrane dynamics.

Global banks sustain losses amounting to billions annually due to fraud. To detect these crimes and uncover new schemes, graph analysis is employed to decipher complex transaction patterns. This study examines these graphs within real-world transaction data by isolating and evaluating network motifs, with a specific emphasis on heterogeneous motifs given the varied nature of banking structures. We introduce a new randomization method capable of producing valid synthetic banking graphs. Findings from the exploration indicate that identifying network motifs yields both deep interpretive value and actionable insights.

This study introduces updated, fully general-relativistic calculations of radiation emitted during the tidal disruption of a white dwarf, specifically investigating scenarios where the object is accreted by an intermediate- or supermassive black hole. We explore how radiative momentum influences subsequent dynamics under various accretion models, employing 1D general-relativistic hydrodynamics that incorporate radiative transfer in the form of the closure $\beta = P_{\rm rad}/E_{\rm rad}$ (where $P_{\rm rad}$ and $E_{\rm rad}$ represent radiation pressure and energy density). We examine two radiation-trapping schemes (diffusion and Trappett 2015 ("Trappett")) alongside two ejection scenarios (adiabatic and radiation-driven). Initially focusing on equatorial tidal encounters, we analyze how accretion dynamics alter event compared to non-radiative cases, noting that all investigated radiation models reduce mass accretion by at least an order of magnitude. Specifically, when Trappett diffusion models accretion is diminished across a broad range of black hole masses, whereas in a purely radiative ejection case, significant reductions only occur for intermediate-mass black holes. We further evaluate the impact of irradiation within dynamical contexts, discovering that although irradiation can expand tidal arms, its effect remains minor due to the compact nature of white dwarfs, which results in confined radiation pressure forces. Semileptonic $\tau$-decays involving three particles provide opportunities for probing intrinsic properties of light hadrons and examining violations of CP symmetry, potentially through the search for electric dipole moments. Since the characteristic q$^2$ range accessible in $\tau$-mode three-particle final states has not yet seen extensive exploration, the theoretical framework for general hadronic processes must be established. This paper extends a previously introduced formalism to accommodate $N$-particle final states. We present a comprehensive theoretical description of three-hadron final states, incorporating spin-violation effects. Specific formation probabilities have also been calculated for several elementary processes characterizing this decay spectrum, enabling precise prediction and analysis via experimental data comparison.

Current motion deblurring algorithms rooted in deep learning typically require vast collections of paired blurry and sharp images, which are difficult to acquire given the inverse blur mechanism inherent in their operation, where one cannot simply compose clear images to create blurry variants. While traditional synthetic methods generate blur data via programming, these methods often consume excessive computational resources and lack the versatility to integrate with diverse architectures, resulting in a bottleneck in training efficiency. To address this, we introduce a conditional generative adversarial network designed specifically for the synthesis of blur images. This proposal decouples the generation process into two stages: first creating coarse blurry images, then refining them to yield final outputs. By handling both upscaling and synthesis in separate passes, this approach offers greater flexibility. Furthermore, equipped with a blur-specific adversarial loss, this network effectively generates realistic blur images, eliminating the artificial boundaries or textures that typically plague synthetic datasets. Empirical evaluations indicate that our method significantly outperforms existing synthetic approaches in performance. In the motion deblurring domain, integrating this synthetic blur dataset into the LRDeblur architecture yields measurable improvements. In image super-resolution, such a dataset enhances the PR-DCR metric by an additional 0.23 compared to using only clear-sharp image pairs. Ultimately, incorporating synthetic datasets into tasks involving natural image restoration represents a promising direction for further performance gains.

Hebbian learning is a form of system self-association that enables autonomous functions by enabling self-learning through direct interaction with the environment without requiring feedback. Because of this property, it serves as an appropriate mechanism for implementing autonomous agents like robots, grounded autonomous systems like space probes, and other analogous applications where interaction occurs. While prior research focused on using this approach for visual tasks such as pattern recognition and edge and orientation detection, there has been little exploration regarding its use in simulation environments without feedback. This paper presents an investigation into Hebbian learning within a robot leg control simulation based on multi-legged robots. Using a leg setup with four legs interacting with a rough terrain, we observed that Hebbian learning improves walking stability significantly compared to a non-learned baseline controller, reducing falls from 17 to 3. Additionally, we observed a reduction in energy requirements, indicated by motor current, from 3.43A to 2.95A, suggesting a more efficient g pattern.

Scientific research relies heavily on sharing datasets through repositories that facilitate discovery through search and visual browsing. Yet, very few data are actually tagged with controlled vocabularies like本体 (ontologies), despite these standards helping define concepts clearly and reveal hidden relationships within and between data collections. We propose using Automatic Information Extraction (AIE) techniques to pull metadata from papers and other sources specifically for tagging data during submission processes. By doing so, we can actively improve ontology tagging standards, thereby enhancing data finding capabilities and supporting cross-validation of results—outcomes directly linked to increased data reusability. Through a detailed case study involving automated AIE on PDFs to extract information for a neuroscience imaging ontology, we identified numerous refinements. These adjustments address fundamental issues within the current automated extraction methods and highlight necessary developments in both data curation practices and automated curation tools.

Hadwiger's well-known conjecture posits that any graph requiring $k$ colors in its chromatic number possesses a $k$-clique minor. Building on this, we analyze a variant where minor definitions are restricted to those generated by applying $l$-tricks (or $l$-reductions), where $l$ is any natural number, thereby creating what is termed the "light version" of the original conjecture, now dependent on two parameters: $k$ and $l$. By re-examining these problems through the lens of model-theory and classifying them according to their complexity, we establish upper bounds on how many colors are needed to guarantee a $k$-clique minor of any size in terms of $k$. We also introduce a specific class of graphs where the "light version" holds true only if $l=0$, demonstrating such problems exist and can be infinitely extensive.

While deriving the core algorithm, an adaptive kernel width learning approach is also proposed; simulation results demonstrate this method supersedes fixed-width strategies, particularly in terms of convergence speed and error correction. Further established is a theoretical framework for the linear approximation of this algorithm's weight updates within a simple graph setting. Consequently, linear regression serves as a basis to formulate solvability conditions and determine the persistent stable region associated with its weight evolution.

Recent advances in Deep Learning have introduced Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNN), which utilize specialized convolution layers to extract local features within graph data. Although highly effective at modeling complex relationships in various applications, these layers remain proprietary secrets within their respective implementations. This paper presents an investigation into viable alternatives. We propose a framework for learning optimal graph convolutional layers as part of the broader GCNN architecture. By searching for a permutation-invariant aggregation function that maps an edge-weighted edge list derived from the input and its neighbor—while maintaining a constant computational complexity of O(c), where c denotes the number of edges in that local window—our method aims to explore the space of aggregation functions beyond the fixed mechanisms currently constrained by standard GCNN designs. Experiments conducted on multiple benchmark graph datasets demonstrate competitive performance comparable to leading methods.

Neural dependency parsing has achieved superior accuracy compared to traditional k-best beam search methods employed in probabilistic constituency parsing. Nevertheless, neural approaches face challenges in acquiring sufficiently large labeled datasets. To address this, we propose an adaptive algorithm capable of self-instructing itself for parsing without external guidance by effectively utilizing its own parsing capabilities to generate dependencies. Specifically, we propose an algorithm for parsing dependency trees that utilizes self-generated information in a dependency tree search method with a constrained beam search that has the suppressed dependencies filtering consideration for preventing cyclic dependencies in structures and a dependent dependency selection method for allowing dependency trees to be learned recursively from its own ability. Experiments utilizing this approach demonstrate that sufficiently large annotated datasets are not required, as adequate data can be synthesized through this method.

This study investigates the transition form factors $f_+(q^2)$, $f_0(q^2)$, and $f_0(-)$ associated with the exclusive semileptonic decays of $b \to u$ quarks via $B_\ell^+\to D^{(*)}q^+$ using the sum rule approach. By employing these sum rules, we analyze quark mass ambiguities and examine the influence of the inclusive decay $B \ell^+\ell^-$ on them. Furthermore, we examine how variations arising from $b \ell^+\ell^-$ contribute to the transition form factors. By comparing our outcomes with experimental observations and theoretical frameworks, we assess the precision of the predicted spectrum $b \ell^+\ell^-$ for the mass range of interest. We also investigate potential contributions from unknown operators to the sum framework.

Eu2Ir2O7, a proposed Weyl semimetal, exhibits an insulator-to-metal transition linked to the substitution of Bismuth for Europium. This study employs a density functional theory approach to explore the physical mechanisms driving this transition. We performed *ab initio* calculations for the Eu2Ir2O7 and Bi2Ir2O7 compounds, utilizing a linear interpolation method to model a solid solution with the formula Eu2-xBixIr2O7. Our results indicate that the Bi→Eu back donation plays a critical role in reducing the energy gap between the valence and conduction bands. Furthermore, these findings suggest the transition is governed by chemical doping via the (Bi/Eu)-f electrons rather than by band structure strain effects.
